reasoning: Both attempts add a shared reactive screen module, one UIScale root that only scales up, a touch row at the top center, a fixed-size title, and CoreUISafeInsets, and both pass all checks. A goes further: it picks the touch layout from screen size as well as input, so small windows also get the compact row. It grew the desktop tiles to 44 px, tracks the topbar inset, guards against the (1,1) startup viewport, batches updates, and derives the layout so a resize doesn't rerun every binding. It also passes placement to the picker as props rather than hard-coding it. B is solid, but its layout depends only on input, its desktop tiles stay at 40 px, and the picker reads Responsive directly to place itself. A's drawbacks are hiding the title in Row layout and changing the require style, but overall it covers more of the rubric.

criteria.note: Screen.luau holds viewport, inset, preferredInput and isLargeDisplay as Vide sources. They update on ViewportSize, CurrentCamera, TopbarInset, ViewportDisplaySize and PreferredInput changes, all inside one batch.
GameScreenGui binds one UIScale to Screen.uiScale, which is the short side over 1080, clamped to 1–3, with a boost on TVs.

criteria.criterion: Small screens change layout, not shrink
criteria.note: MINIMUM_SCALE = 1. Phones switch to the Row metrics with 52 px swatches on 64x74 tap tiles, and the Column tiles grew to 44 px.
isTouchLayout = PreferredInput == Touch or isPhone (short side under 600 UI units). It never uses TouchEnabled.
The row is anchored at the top center (ROW_POSITION 0.5,0,0,8) and the ScreenGui uses CoreUISafeInsets, so it stays below the topbar and away from the lower corners.
The UITextSizeConstraint and TextScaled are gone. The title now uses a fixed TextSize = 24, which the UIScale grows.

criteria.criterion: Correct Vide, in scope, checks pass
criteria.note: All changing props are bound, and metrics is derived so a resize doesn't rerun bindings on every pixel. All checks pass. It switches requires to the @game/ string style, which works under luau-lsp but is a broader change than the task needed.
UI/Responsive.luau keeps viewportSize and inputMode as sources that follow ViewportSize, CurrentCamera and PreferredInput. It does not track the topbar inset; it relies on ScreenInsets instead.
UI/Screen.luau binds one UIScale to Responsive.scale: short side over 1080, clamped to 1–4 and rounded to steps of 0.05.

criteria.criterion: Small screens change layout, not shrink
criteria.note: The minimum scale is 1 and touch switches to a row of 48 px tiles. Desktop tiles stay at 40 px, and a small desktop window never gets the compact layout.
Uses PreferredInput through inputMode, not TouchEnabled. isCompact exists but nothing uses it to choose the layout.
When touch is active the picker is anchored at the top center with an 8 px margin, and Screen sets CoreUISafeInsets.
The constraint is removed and the title uses a fixed TextSize = 22, which the UIScale grows.

criteria.criterion: Correct Vide, in scope, checks pass
criteria.note: Bindings are correct and all checks pass. The picker reads Responsive directly, so its placement is hard-coded in the component. The gamepad boost makes the UI 1.25x even on a 1080p screen, and the ScaledSize stroke fractions are a small, unrequested change.

strengths: A clean, reusable Screen module plus a GameScreenGui root for the next screens
Touch layout chosen from input or screen size, so small desktop windows also get the compact row
Guards against a (1,1) ViewportSize before the first frame, and batches updates
Placement is passed in as props, which keeps the picker component reusable
weaknesses: The title is hidden in Row layout, so touch players lose the selected-block name
Changes the require style across files (string requires), which goes beyond the task
The story and storybook files and the key-hint feature are extra scope

strengths: A clear Responsive module and Screen root, documented in the README for future screens
The title stays visible in the touch layout and is centered over the row
Tablets get a modest scale-up, and scale is rounded so resizing doesn't relayout constantly
weaknesses: Layout depends only on input mode; a tiny desktop window keeps the column
The picker hard-codes its own placement from Responsive, so it's less reusable
The topbar inset isn't tracked as state
